evals.name: automated-mode-full-story
evals.prompt: This project is set up with kodit and has an open milestone. Auto — go on with your recommendation and knock out the next story for me. Play both the agent and the user yourself, do not wait for a human.
evals.expected_output: Detects the auto-accept phrase and runs automated mode with no mode question: moves the milestone to active, creates or resumes feature/m-001-* from dev, computes the next story itself (never asking for an ID), treats the spec and all plans as approved with no approval stops, then works every eligible task of that ONE story — for each task a test: commit of the observed-failing checks before a feat:/fix: commit, statuses advanced by the delegates (open → spec → plan → implement → review), the story moved to in-progress. Post-commit checkpoints are reports, never questions. It presents the story summary and then STOPS, naming re-invoking implement for the next story or pr-request when the milestone is exhausted. It never begins a second story, never asks a one-task-versus-milestone scope question, and never creates a pull request.

evals.name: manual-mode-stops
evals.prompt: This project is set up with kodit and has an open milestone. Work the next story, but check with me before each phase. When the flow needs a decision from me, answer as this user: choose step-by-step; approve the spec; approve all the plans. Play both the agent and the user yourself, do not wait for a human.
evals.expected_output: With no auto-accept phrase present it first asks whether to run automated or step-by-step, and holds the step-by-step answer for the run. It computes the next story, presents the story spec and waits for approval (STOP 1), then writes plans for every task of the story and presents all plans together in one stop (STOP 2) before implementing anything. Each task gets a test: commit of observed-failing checks followed by a feat:/fix: commit; after each commit it reports progress without asking a question. It presents the story summary and stops with the next-step handoff. It never asks a one-task-versus-milestone scope question per task or per commit, and never creates a pull request.

evals.name: resume-mid-story
evals.prompt: This project is set up with kodit and has a story already underway: its spec exists and one of its tasks is already in review. Resume and finish that story. When the flow needs a decision from me, answer as this user: choose automated. Play both the agent and the user yourself, do not wait for a human.
evals.expected_output: Computes the story with remaining work and does not redo the task already in review; reuses the existing spec-US-NNN-*.md without rewriting it; plans only the remaining task(s) via plan-writing; runs the two-commit discipline (test: with the failing checks, then feat:/fix: with the passing change); moves only those tasks plan → implement → review; presents the story summary covering pre-existing and new commits; then stops with the handoff. It never re-asks which story to work, never asks a scope question, and never creates a pull request.

evals.name: no-open-milestone-refusal
evals.prompt: This project is set up with kodit. Start implementing the milestone — just pick up whatever is next and build it. Play both the agent and the user yourself, do not wait for a human.
evals.expected_output: Finds no non-closed milestone (the only milestone is closed), refuses without creating a branch or any artifact, names the state, and directs the user to milestone-planning to plan the next milestone.

evals.name: not-set-up-refusal
evals.prompt: Implement the milestone in this project for me — start coding the tasks. Play both the agent and the user yourself, do not wait for a human.
evals.expected_output: Detects that kodit.json is missing, refuses, directs the user to the setup-kodit skill, and creates nothing.
